key: Whosoever doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, him verily we shall quicken with good life, and We shall pay them a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do.
s: After warning against trading God’s covenant for small gain, the surah turns to reward; al-Tabari, on 16:97, takes the good life as contentment, the reading he prefers among several, since one made content with his portion is not troubled chasing what escapes him.
src: Al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 16:97, Tarteel QUL Arabic text via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

evidence.words: وأولى الأقوال بالصواب قول من قال: تأويل ذلك: فلنحيينه حياة طيبة بالقناعة، وذلك أن من قنعه الله بما قسم له من رزق لم يكثر للدنيا تعبه، ولم يعظم فيها نَصَبه ولم يتكدّر فيها عيشه باتباعه بغية ما فاته منها وحرصه على ما لعله لا يدركه فيها
evidence.gloss: The most correct of the sayings is that of those who said: its interpretation is, We shall give him a good life through contentment; for one whom God makes content with the provision He has allotted him does not multiply his toil for the world, his weariness in it does not grow great, and his living in it is not troubled by pursuing what has escaped him of it and craving what he may never attain in it.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, An-Nahl 16:97, at 1997), one whole sentence of the ayah, 37 words. Plain sense faithful: 16:95 forbids purchasing a small gain at the price of Allah’s covenant, and 16:96 to 16:97 turn to recompense; no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 16:97 al-Tabari reports five readings with their chains (lawful provision, contentment, a life of faith and obedience, happiness, the Garden), then in his own voice prefers contentment and gives the reason the sentence paraphrases; he also argues from the context of 16:94 to 16:96. The reading is his, stated as his preference, without drift. Evidence is one contiguous span. 43 words; entry-check ok.
